extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners (attorneys/agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive guidance for examiners (and practitioners) on Request for Continued Examination (RCE) practice, improper RCE consequences, post-Board and post-appeal handling, and general examiner duties in office actions (citation, rejections, and reasons for allowance).

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE eligibility (application and filing dates)
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible for continued examination under 37 CFR 1.114, the application must be a utility or plant application filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) on or after June 8, 1995, or an international application filed under 35 U.S.C. 363 on or after June 8, 1995. The RCE must be filed on or after May 29, 2000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This eligibility requirement is repeated in multiple form paragraphs and examiner notes (e.g., ¶ 7.42.10–7.42.16, ¶ 7.42.07). If the application does not meet these filing-date/type thresholds, RCE practice under 37 CFR 1.114 does not apply and a PTO-2051 Notice of Improper Request for Continued Examination should be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE filing requirements (prosecution closed; submission and fee)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prosecution in the application must be closed. A submission and a fee are required at the time the RCE is filed. If reply to an Office action under 35 U.S.C. 132 is outstanding (e.g., final rejection), the submission must meet the reply requirements of 37 CFR 1.111. If there is no outstanding Office action, the submission can be an information disclosure statement, an amendment, new arguments, or new evidence. The submission may be a previously filed amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing qualifications and requirements are summarized in the Instruction Sheet for RCEs. A request for suspension of action under 37 CFR 1.103(c) does not satisfy the submission requirement. The RCE fee under 37 CFR 1.17(e) is required when the RCE is filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of improper RCE (general rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an RCE is filed but lacks the fee required by 37 CFR 1.17(e) and/or the submission required by 37 CFR 1.114, the examiner should treat the request as an improper RCE and withdraw the appeal pursuant to 37 CFR 1.114(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an RCE is improper, the submission generally will not be entered (see ¶ 7.42.16). Use the appropriate form paragraph (e.g., 7.42.10–7.42.16) to notify applicant. If the application is not eligible for RCE practice, technical support should prepare PTO-2051 to notify applicant that continued examination does not apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of improper RCE when application is under appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: If an improper RCE is filed while the application is under appeal, withdrawal of the appeal results in either allowance or abandonment depending on the status of the claims: if no claim is allowed, the application is abandoned; if there is at least one allowed claim, the application should be passed to issue on the allowed claim(s). Claims allowable only by virtue of dependency upon rejected claims are treated as rejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon withdrawal, proceedings as to the rejected claims are considered terminated. See MPEP § 1215.01. Use form paragraphs (e.g., ¶ 7.42.10, 7.42.11, 7.42.13) tailored to whether claims are allowed and whether submissions/fees are missing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper RCE does NOT toll statutory time periods
rubrics_metrics.description: An improper RCE will not toll any time period. Before appeal: if RCE is improper and prosecution is not closed, the time period set forth in the last Office action will continue to run and the application will be abandoned after the statutory time period if no timely reply is filed. Under appeal: an improper RCE withdraws the appeal but does not toll time periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warnings in the Instruction Sheet emphasize that no additional time will be given to correct an improper RCE; examiners should state that any time period running was not tolled by the filing of the improper request in the notice (¶ 7.42.16).

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry of submissions filed with an improper RCE (exception rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: In general, if a submission was filed with an improper RCE, it should not be entered. An exception exists for an amendment which obviously places the application in condition for allowance; such an amendment may be entered with the approval of the supervisory patent examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the fee is missing but a submission is filed, the examiner should state whether or not the submission has been entered (e.g., “The submission filed with the improper RCE has not been entered.”). See MPEP § 1214.07 for handling entries after Board decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE filed after Board decision but before further appeal/civil action (proper RCE)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an RCE (accompanied by fee and a submission) is filed after a Board decision but before filing a Notice of Appeal to the Federal Circuit or commencement of a civil action, and is otherwise timely, the appeal will be withdrawn pursuant to 37 CFR 1.114 and prosecution in the application is reopened; the applicant’s submission will be entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 7.42.07 should be used to notify applicant that the appeal has been withdrawn and prosecution reopened. Generally, the time for filing notice of appeal or commencing civil action is within two months of the Board's decision (37 CFR 1.304 and MPEP § 1216).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of Board decision as law of the case
rubrics_metrics.description: A Board decision in an application has res judicata effect and is the 'law of the case,' and is thus controlling in that application and any subsequent, related application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Board entered a new ground of rejection pursuant to 37 CFR 1.196(b), argument alone (without amendment of the rejected claims or submission of a showing of facts) will not remove such rejection because the examiner lacks authority to allow the claims absent amendment or a showing of facts not before the Board (see MPEP §§ 706.03(w), 1214.01).

rubrics_metrics.name: Shortened statutory period to correct formal matters when passing to issue
rubrics_metrics.description: If the application will be passed to issue on allowed claim(s) but formal matters are outstanding, applicant should be given a shortened statutory period of ONE MONTH or THIRTY DAYS, whichever is longer, to correct the formal matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraphs 7.42.12 and 7.42.14 describe this practice. Extensions of time may be granted under 37 CFR 1.136. Explain the specific formal matters to be corrected in the notice (bracketed text).

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE unavailable after appeal to Federal Circuit or civil action unless terminated
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.114 practice is not available after filing of a Notice of Appeal to the Federal Circuit or commencement of a civil action, unless the appeal or civil action is terminated and the application is still pending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an RCE is filed after court review, the examiner should bring the application to the attention of the supervisory patent examiner or special program examiner to determine whether the RCE is proper. Unless the application contains allowed claims (or the court’s mandate indicates further Office action), termination of an unsuccessful appeal or civil action results in abandonment (see MPEP § 1216.01).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner duty to make a thorough study and prior art investigation (37 CFR 1.104)
rubrics_metrics.description: On taking up an application for examination, the examiner shall make a thorough study thereof and shall make a thorough investigation of the available prior art relating to the subject matter of the claimed invention. The examination shall be complete with respect both to compliance with applicable statutes and rules and to the patentability of the invention as claimed, as well as with respect to matters of form, unless otherwise indicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An international-type search will be made for national applications filed on/after June 1, 1978; an international-type search report can be prepared upon request and fee. In appropriate circumstances (e.g., misjoinder, fundamental defects) the examiner's action may be limited to certain matters before further action is taken; matters of form need not be raised until a claim is found allowable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office action must notify reasons and provide useful information (37 CFR 1.104(b),(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant will be notified of the examiner’s action. The reasons for any adverse action or any objection or requirement will be stated in an Office action and such information or references will be given as may be useful in aiding the applicant to judge the propriety of continuing the prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For rejections under 35 U.S.C. 103, the way a reference is modified or how plural references are combined should be set out. When necessary, include particular figures, pages, paragraphs, or relevant comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection citation standard (cite best references; identify parts relied on)
rubrics_metrics.description: In rejecting claims for want of novelty or for obviousness, the examiner must cite the best references at his or her command. When a reference is complex or shows or describes inventions other than that claimed, the particular part relied on must be designated as nearly as practicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The pertinence of each reference, if not apparent, must be clearly explained and each rejected claim specified. In exceptional or pro se cases, a more complete explanation may be needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliance on admissions and facts within examiner's knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: In rejecting claims the examiner may rely upon admissions by the applicant (or patent owner in reexamination proceedings), and may also rely upon facts within his or her knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a rejection is based on facts within the personal knowledge of an Office employee, the data shall be as specific as possible and the reference must be supported, when called for by the applicant, by the affidavit of such employee; such affidavit shall be subject to contradiction or explanation by affidavits of the applicant and other persons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of subject matter developed by another as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 103
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject matter developed by another person which qualifies as prior art only under 35 U.S.C. 102(e), (f) or (g) may be used as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 103 against a claimed invention unless the entire rights to the subject matter and the claimed invention were commonly owned by the same person or organization or subject to an obligation of assignment to the same person or organization at the time the claimed invention was made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An exception for joint research agreements applies if (A) the claimed invention was made by or on behalf of parties to a joint research agreement in effect on or before the date the claimed invention was made; (B) the claimed invention resulted from activities within the scope of the joint research agreement; and (C) the application discloses or is amended to disclose the names of the parties to the joint research agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection preclusion by published statutory invention registration
rubrics_metrics.description: The claims in any original application naming an inventor will be rejected as being precluded by a waiver in a published statutory invention registration naming that inventor if the same subject matter is claimed in the application and the statutory invention registration. Similar rule for reissue applications seeking to claim subject matter waived in the statutory invention registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The two-part test for reissue applications includes (i) subject matter not covered by claims issued prior to the date of publication, and (ii) same subject matter waived in the statutory invention registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: When domestic patents are cited, their numbers and dates and patentee names will be stated. If domestic patent application publications are cited, include publication number, publication date, and applicant names. For foreign published applications or patents, state nationality/country, numbers, dates, names of patentees, and other necessary data. If only part of a document is involved, identify particular pages/sheets. For printed publications include author (if any), title, date, pages/plates, and place of publication or where a copy can be found.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide sufficient data to enable applicant or patent owner to identify the cited documents; include particular figures/pages when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasons for allowance must be set forth when unclear
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner believes that the record of prosecution as a whole does not make clear his or her reasons for allowing a claim or claims, the examiner may set forth such reasoning. The reasons shall be incorporated into an Office action rejecting other claims or be the subject of a separate communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The applicant or patent owner may file a statement commenting on the reasons for allowance within a specified time. Failure by the examiner to respond to any such statement does not give rise to any implication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office action attachments and forms
rubrics_metrics.description: The list of references cited appears on a separate form, Notice of References Cited, PTO-892, attached to applicant’s copies of the action. Where applicable, other forms (e.g., PTO-948, PTO-152) are attached to the first action. Attachments have the same paper number and are to be considered as part of the Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat attachments as integral parts of the Office action; ensure correct paper numbering and inclusion with applicant copies.

rubrics_metrics.name: First action procedure and examiner-initiated discussions
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the current first action procedure, the examiner signifies on the Office Action Summary Form PTOL-326 the period set for reply, any attachments, and a 'Summary of Action.' The examiner may indicate that a discussion with the applicant’s or patent owner’s representative may result in agreements whereby the application may be placed in condition for allowance and will telephone the representative within about 2 weeks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resulting amendments may be made by applicant’s attorney/agent or by examiner in an examiner’s amendment. When extensive amendments are necessary, it is preferable that attorney/agent file them to provide a better file wrapper record and reduce Office workload.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply filing format guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Replies to Office actions should include the application number as well as the 4-digit art unit number and the examiner’s name to expedite handling within the Office. Applicants are encouraged to include the 4-digit confirmation number on every paper filed in the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 503 for explanation of the confirmation number. Proper identification speeds processing and reduces clerical errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for 35 U.S.C. 132 notifications and 103 explanations
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever, on examination, any claim for a patent is rejected, notification of the reasons for rejection and/or objection together with such information and references as may be useful in judging the propriety of continuing the prosecution (35 U.S.C. 132) should be given. For rejections under 35 U.S.C. 103, the way in which a reference is modified or plural references are combined should be set out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include specific figures, pages, or paragraphs of references when necessary. In exceptional cases and in pro se cases where the inventor is unfamiliar with patent law and practice, a more complete explanation may be needed.
